sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17 (English text). Relevant text: SQL Server 2016 and later match a SAS credential named after the container URL (IDENTITY = 'SHARED ACCESS SIGNATURE'); error 3201 'Cannot open backup device ... Operating system error 50(The request is not supported.)', one cause 'The policy assigned to the SAS token expired'; fix: create a new SAS token (from a new policy) and re-create or alter the credential; remove a leading '?'. The SQL Server page 'View or change the recovery model of a database' (read 2026-11-18): after switching to simple, 'Discontinue any scheduled jobs for backing up the transaction log'; after switching back to full, 'take a full or differential database backup to start the log chain' because the switch 'takes effect only after the first data backup'. The SQL Agent alert and operator commands in the case are authored renderings.

brief.situation: You are the database administrator at Haldane Freight. SQL Server 2022 on an Azure VM (sqlvm01) hosts the billing database in FULL recovery. An Agent job backs up its log to Azure Blob Storage every 15 minutes. Today a disk alert fired: the log drive L: is 94% full and growing about 1% every 8 minutes. If the log fills, billing stops accepting writes.
handover: The storage team rotated SAS policies on the backup container on Saturday.
The job has no operator notification; nobody was told it failed.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the billing database's log, the Agent job that backs it up and the storage container it writes to.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

newsas.label: Re-create the URL credential with a SAS from the new policy, then run the log backup job now
newsas.available: not busy and (not fixed and not harmed)
newsas.why: Already done, or the system is down.

effects.output:
dba@sqlvm01:~$ sqlcmd -Q "ALTER CREDENTIAL [https://sqlbkp.blob.core.windows.net/backups] WITH IDENTITY = 'SHARED ACCESS SIGNATURE', SECRET = '<new SAS from sql-backup-2026q4, no leading ?>'"
dba@sqlvm01:~$ sqlcmd -Q "EXEC msdb.dbo.sp_start_job 'billing-log-backup'"
Job 'billing-log-backup' started successfully.

effects.log: The job can write again; the first backup carries two days of log, after which the log is reused and stops growing. The chain is unbroken, so point-in-time restore still covers the whole period.

alert.label: Add an operator notification on failure for every backup job, and a SQL Agent alert on error 3201
alert.available: not busy and (not planned and not harmed)
alert.why: Already done, or the system is down.

effects.output:
dba@sqlvm01:~$ sqlcmd -Q "EXEC msdb.dbo.sp_update_job @job_name='billing-log-backup', @notify_level_email=2, @notify_email_operator_name='DBA-oncall'" (and the other 6 backup jobs)
dba@sqlvm01:~$ sqlcmd -Q "EXEC msdb.dbo.sp_add_alert @name='Backup device error 3201', @message_id=3201, @severity=0"; sp_add_notification ... 'DBA-oncall'

effects.log: A failed backup now pages the on-call DBA the first time, not when a disk fills days later; the storage team is asked to announce SAS rotations to the DBAs.

effects.log: The drive empties, and the log backup chain is broken: there is no point-in-time restore for billing until a new full backup, and the last two days are covered only by Saturday's full.

writeup.question: For the record: why the log grew, how you fixed it without losing recoverability, and how the next failure gets noticed.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects the full log to the failing job.
parts.modelAnswer: log_reuse_wait_desc was LOG_BACKUP: the log waited for a backup. The Agent job had failed every run since Saturday 02:15 with error 3201, because its URL credential held a SAS from a policy removed in Saturday's rotation.

parts.label: Fix
parts.modelAnswer: Altered the credential with a SAS from the new policy and ran the job; the log was backed up and reused. Switching to SIMPLE would have broken the log chain and point-in-time restore.

parts.label: Noticed
parts.modelAnswer: Every backup job now emails the on-call operator on failure and an Agent alert fires on error 3201; the storage team will announce SAS rotations.

expertPath.text: LOG_BACKUP; job failing since Saturday with 3201; credential from a removed policy; no notification.
Alter the credential with the new SAS; run the job; notifications and a 3201 alert.
Job succeeded; reuse wait NOTHING; L: 41%.

chainBroken.headline: Free space bought with recoverability
chainBroken.body: The log was full because it was waiting for a backup. Fix the backup (here, the expired SAS) and the log is reused; switching to SIMPLE throws away the ability to restore to a point in time.

logFull.headline: LOG_BACKUP means a backup is missing
logFull.body: log_reuse_wait_desc told you what the log waits for. The job's history told you why it was not happening: the backup URL's credential.

chainKept.headline: Good: fixed the job, not the symptom
chainKept.body: You read why the log could not be reused and why the job failed, replaced the expired SAS, ran the job, checked the drive, and made failures visible the first time.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up

scoring.modelReasoning: The log waits for a log backup, and the backup job has failed since Saturday with error 3201 because its credential holds a SAS from a policy the storage team removed. Re-create the credential with a SAS from the new policy and run the job now: the log is backed up, reused, and the chain stays intact. SIMPLE recovery frees space by destroying point-in-time recovery; restarting Agent changes nothing. Then make backup failures notify someone.
